item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-b08a7e013b9038f5","start_unit":20,"end_unit":23,"fact_summary":"On October 28, 2023, at least 27 journalists covering opposition and ruling-party rallies in Dhaka were attacked or harassed by BNP supporters, Awami League supporters, and police; police used tear gas, sound grenades, and rubber bullets while dispersing protesters, and journalists suffered beatings, equipment damage, and injuries.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.6","3B.3","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 political rallies.","ruler_attribution":"The report identifies police and ruling Awami League supporters among perpetrators and places the events within opposition demands that Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina step down; it does not establish her personal orders or knowledge.","limitations":["Accountability outcomes were not reported by November 1, 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e0be1813b5ee9fde","start_unit":14,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"Bangladesh officials coordinated with Myanmar junta authorities on a 2023 pilot effort to repatriate about 1,100 Rohingya refugees, including a May go-and-see visit, without consulting the community or resolving risks to safety, citizenship, movement, land, and livelihoods. Refugees reported coercion, surveillance, and harassment by Bangladesh administrators and intelligence officers, although the government stated returns would not be forced and Bangladesh had generally respected nonrefoulement since 2017.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.5","2B.7","3B.7","3B.9","6B.3","6B.6","6B.8","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns Bangladesh policy and events in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the policy to Bangladesh authorities and the refugee relief administration; it does not specifically document Sheikh Hasina's personal decision-making.","limitations":["The account relies substantially on refugee interviews and Human Rights Watch assessment.","It records an official assurance against forced return alongside allegations of coercive conditions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ac14fd2d3c6d59f3","start_unit":23,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"A Bangladesh Cabinet Division framework published in June 2023 institutionalized results-based monitoring for the National Social Security Strategy: annual reports were prepared for the Central Management Committee and submitted to the relevant Parliamentary Standing Committee, with the stated purpose of using evidence to improve efficiency, effectiveness, poverty reduction, inequality reduction, and continuous performance.","question_ids":["5B.7","6B.1","6B.2","6B.5","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Framework prepared in June 2023; implementation evidence is institutional rather than outcome-specific.","ruler_attribution":"The framework was prepared by the Cabinet Division under the Government of Bangladesh; it supports attribution to the governing administration but not necessarily to Hasina personally.","limitations":["The supplied page describes the framework and reporting structure, not verified 2023 results or corrective actions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-95bd190439d38be0","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"JusticeMakers Bangladesh reported 148 law-enforcement-attributed torture, extrajudicial-killing, and degrading-treatment incidents during 2023 affecting 1,842 people, including 31 incidents causing 34 deaths and 108 incidents causing injuries to 1,788 people. BNP members accounted for 51 incidents affecting 1,453 people, and only 10 victims or family members filed criminal cases; 128 incidents affecting 1,832 victims produced no legal action because of intimidation or other barriers.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Annual report covers January through December 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes incidents to law-enforcement agencies during Hasina's administration; it does not prove her personal participation or knowledge.","limitations":["This is an NGO monitoring report based on online news monitoring, not a judicially established case file.","The report does not establish responsibility for each incident or government response to each allegation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-30d2c717f980c76f","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"At a October 5, 2023 ceremony for Russia's handover of nuclear fuel to the Rooppur plant, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina stated Bangladesh would use nuclear energy solely for peace, supported worldwide nuclear disarmament and a total ban on nuclear weapons, and said Bangladesh had legislation overseeing the nuclear industry and an agreement for Russia to take back and reprocess spent fuel.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.3","1B.4","1B.7","1B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Direct statement and arrangements dated October 5, 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributed to Sheikh Hasina.","limitations":["The source reports stated policy and agreements, not independent verification of implementation, funding, inspections, or operational safety."]},{"source_id":"SRC-75a3a58586e367d3","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"CIVICUS reported that in 2023 Bangladesh's civic space was downgraded to 'closed' after a government crackdown on opposition politicians, human-rights defenders, protesters, journalists, and critics involving intimidation, violence, arrest, torture, media shutdowns, and a Cyber Security Act retaining much of the Digital Security Act's repressive language. It reported almost 10,000 opposition activists arrested after the October 28 BNP rally, over 5,500 injured, and at least 16 people killed in ongoing violence.","question_ids":["2B.3","2B.4","2B.6","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","4B.8","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Report posted December 14, 2023 and describes events throughout 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the crackdown to Bangladesh authorities and links it to the government's conduct before the January 2024 election; it does not establish Hasina's personal orders for every act.","limitations":["Some figures are reported findings of Human Rights Watch or UN experts cited by CIVICUS.","The account includes allegations and does not adjudicate individual criminal responsibility."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f120e30c0a7481e2","start_unit":14,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch documented 26 cases of murder, kidnapping, torture, rape, sexual assault, and forced marriage against Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh during evidence collection from January to April 2023. Authorities were described as failing to provide adequate protection, accessible complaint systems, investigation, prosecution, police access, and medical or legal assistance; only three cases led to arrests.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.3","6B.6","6B.8","7B.9","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Evidence collection and publication are within 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report concerns Bangladesh authorities and specifically references Sheikh Hasina's prior pledges, but does not establish her personal direction of camp security.","limitations":["The cases are documented by Human Rights Watch through interviews and supporting records, not all adjudicated in court.","The violence was largely attributed to armed groups and criminal gangs, with state failures and alleged collusion as qualifying context."]},{"source_id":"SRC-62a5c4d126eca104","start_unit":13,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"UNICEF reported that in 2023, following advocacy with Bangladesh's Ministry of Health, UNICEF piloted locally produced ready-to-use therapeutic food to combat severe wasting, especially in Rohingya camps; the report also describes UNICEF's broader 2023 work on child protection, WASH, social protection, and disaster preparedness.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.6","6B.8","6B.9","6B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"UNICEF reports actions and partnerships during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the Bangladesh pilot to UNICEF advocacy with the Ministry of Health, not directly to Hasina or her cabinet.","limitations":["The report provides no Bangladesh-specific outcome measure for the pilot.","Much of the surrounding material concerns UNICEF globally or regionally rather than Bangladesh."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3a6dfbe08da08b89","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"A 2023 legal study concluded that Bangladesh's Digital Security Act, originally presented as a cybersecurity measure, was used primarily against defamation, sedition, criticism of government officials, and investigative journalism; it characterized the law as broad, selectively applied, and harmful to freedom of speech and media freedom.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.2","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.1","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Study published in June 2023 and evaluates the law's operation relevant to the period.","ruler_attribution":"The study links the law to the government agenda and officials, but does not prove Hasina personally directed individual prosecutions.","limitations":["This is a scholarly qualitative study synthesizing cited primary and secondary sources rather than a new incident dataset.","Some evidence discussed predates 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8de8e695f261a970","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The U.S. State Department reported that in 2023 Bangladesh had credible reports of extrajudicial killings, disappearances, torture, arbitrary detention, serious restrictions on expression and assembly, political prisoners, corruption, and widespread impunity; in most cases the government did not take credible steps to identify and punish officials or security personnel responsible for abuses.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9","5B.5","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Annual country report covers 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report evaluates the Bangladesh government and security forces under Hasina's premiership; it does not establish her personal involvement in each abuse.","limitations":["The report aggregates allegations and findings from multiple sources and does not resolve every individual case."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8de8e695f261a970","start_unit":6,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"During 2023 the government widely used the Digital Security Act against critics, journalists, and online users; more than 7,000 DSA cases were reported pending, and the replacement Cyber Security Act retained police powers to search, seize, and arrest without warrants. Authorities also blocked or slowed internet services around opposition rallies and restricted or removed critical websites and content.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.2","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns laws and enforcement during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the legal and connectivity measures to the government and its regulators; it does not establish Hasina's personal involvement in each restriction.","limitations":["The report includes some data and legal history extending before 2023.","The replacement law was passed in September 2023, near the end of the period."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8de8e695f261a970","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"Bangladesh cooperated with UNHCR and humanitarian organizations to provide substantial assistance to nearly one million registered Rohingya refugees in 2023, including registration, health care, education, and camp management; however, authorities restricted movement, employment, education outside the approved curriculum, and access to services, and accountability for trafficking, torture, killings, and other abuses remained weak.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.7","6B.8","6B.10","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Report covers refugee conditions during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes assistance and restrictions to Bangladesh government institutions; it does not isolate Sheikh Hasina's personal choices.","limitations":["The source records both humanitarian cooperation and serious restrictions or accountability failures.","Some figures and assessments are attributed to international organizations and observers."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d739fcf9562f5b88","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"A 2023 Cambridge University Press study argued that Bangladesh's constitutional identity remains ethnonationalist and exclusionary: the Fifteenth Amendment reinstated a Bengalee identity for the people while Article 23A offers only weak, non-justiciable cultural protection for ethnic communities. The authors linked this framework to continuing exclusion of non-Bengalee groups and incomplete implementation of autonomy and peacebuilding arrangements in the Chittagong Hill Tracts.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","4B.10","6B.3","6B.8","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published in 2023 and evaluates constitutional arrangements relevant to the period.","ruler_attribution":"The study concerns the constitutional order and successive governments, not a specific 2023 act personally taken by Hasina.","limitations":["This is a scholarly constitutional analysis rather than a direct account of Hasina's 2023 conduct.","Its principal legal changes predate the target year."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d94a7e5a704bb819","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Freedom House rated Bangladesh's internet freedom 'Partly Free' at 41/100 in 2023, reporting declining internet freedom, throttling around opposition rallies, physical violence against online activists and journalists, extensive use of the Digital Security Act, and expected tightening of digital controls through proposed content and data regulations.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","7B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Country report covers the 2023 reporting period.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the restrictions to the government, BTRC, and ruling-party-aligned actors; it does not establish Hasina's personal role in each measure.","limitations":["The report's coverage period is June 1, 2022 to May 31, 2023, so it does not cover all of calendar 2023.","The score is Freedom House's country-level assessment, not a ruler-specific finding."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied documents contain no material evidence about Sheikh Hasina's 2023 conduct regarding nuclear proliferation controls, arms transfers, conventional foreign wars, fiscal or monetary policy, personal assets, conflicts of interest, or direct appointment decisions.","Several sources report government-level conditions or institutional actions without establishing Sheikh Hasina's personal knowledge, intent, or orders.","Facts are evidence statements only; no chapter scores are assigned."]}
